clue.text: Know-all clerk writing judgment briefly in right place

indicators.note: the abbreviation R for right is swapped out, the new piece going in its place

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a word said briefly is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a verdict is a judgment, as a jury's

explanation.surface: An office clerk who writes his rulings in the proper spot is mocked as a smart alec.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims VERDICT to VERDIC; 'in right place' puts that where the R (right) of CLERK stood, giving CLE + VERDIC + K.
explanation.definitionFit: A smug person who shows off their cleverness is called a know-all in British slang.

clue.text: Area often screened off, but a lot left visible

parts.note: a lot, as in casting lots, is a matter of chance

explanation.surface: A partitioned area has a large part still on view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visible' only rounds off the surface. A rood screen often divides the nave of a church from the part around the altar.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a church near the altar for clergy and choir is often separated from the nave by a rood screen.

clue.text: Unbiased coins needed for toss-up

parts.note: even means fair, not favouring either side
coins are money

explanation.surface: Fair coins are what a coin toss requires.
explanation.definitionFit: A toss-up is a fifty-fifty chance, which bookmakers price at odds of one to one.

clue.text: Money's of no account, bypass bringing such benefits?

definitions.meaning: a careless attitude to cash, which is easily got and easily lost
a bypass road lets traffic arrive and depart without hold-ups

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: a bypass makes coming and going easy for drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says money gained without effort is spent just as freely, so it counts for little.

clue.text: See Cinders in tatters

indicators.note: something in tatters is torn apart, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A look at the pantomime heroine Cinderella in her rags.
explanation.definitionFit: To see is to perceive or make out, a synonym.

clue.text: Army officer holding old badge of rank

indicators.note: one piece holding another contains it, so the second goes inside

parts.note: a cornet was formerly the lowest commissioned cavalry officer

explanation.surface: A military officer clinging to an outdated insignia.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crown worn or displayed by peers marks their degree of nobility.

clue.text: Took steps to make staff appear on time

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a staff is a rod or stick

explanation.surface: Someone made efforts to get employees to arrive punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees; it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Took steps is the past tense of walk, the same as stepped or walked.

clue.text: Damned healthy looking

definitions.meaning: a mild British swear word, as in 'that blasted dog'
having a fresh red glow in the cheeks

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a British euphemism for bloody and also describes a rosy complexion.

clue.text: Oz girl's taken up to bar, extremely happy

indicators.note: in a down clue taking something up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: a rod is a bar

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A girl from Australia has been taken off to the pub, very cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns TO + ROD into DOROT; 'extremely' adds HY. Oz is also the land in The Wizard of Oz, whose heroine this is, not Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of L. Frank Baum's Wizard of Oz stories bears this name.

clue.text: Ask for debating topic, but reason fallaciously

definitions.meaning: read literally, to request the matter under discussion
to argue in a circle, assuming what is to be proved

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase's strict logical sense is circular reasoning; the first reading takes its words at face value.
explanation.definitionFit: The logical fallacy petitio principii assumes the conclusion in its premise; literally it is to plead for the point at issue.

clue.text: Opposed to cut, protests

indicators.note: a word that is cut loses its final letter

parts.note: averse means opposed to or unwilling

explanation.surface: Against reductions, demonstrations take place.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest that something is so is to assert or declare it firmly.

clue.text: Give in slip, returned in part

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: to sunder is to part or split

indicators.note: a word returned is read backwards

parts.note: to err is to make a slip

explanation.surface: A form is handed in, partly sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ERR into RRE, which goes 'in' SUNDER. 'slip' and 'part' look like nouns but are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield or capitulate is to stop resisting.

clue.text: Admit order to bathe before visit?

definitions.meaning: a command to a guest: arrive, washed

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase into an instruction to arrive having washed.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess the truth after hiding it is a common idiom.

clue.text: Check out the way journeys end for Shakespeare?

parts.note: to try something is to test or check it out
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Investigate the route where trips finish in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelfth Night has 'Journeys end in lovers meeting', so a lovers' meeting is where journeys end for Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret rendezvous between lovers is the meeting the playwright's song names.

clue.text: Lover taking in person making repairs necessary to ring?

definitions.text: person making repairs necessary to ring?

indicators.note: one piece taking another holds it inside

parts.note: leman is an archaic word for a lover
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suitor carrying in a repairman needed for a wedding band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests a wedding ring; it means a telephone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone engineer maintains the wires that let a phone ring.

clue.text: One of Chesterton's men used to swim in river

indicators.note: one piece in another goes inside it

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

indicators.note: letters that swim move about, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from a novel used to go swimming in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swim' signals the anagram, placed 'in' the river. In G. K. Chesterton's The Man Who Was Thursday, the anarchists are named after days of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterton's novel names each member of its secret council after a weekday.

clue.text: Given a jet, be taken up in it — had narrow escape

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed in the word just given

parts.note: douched means sprayed with a jet of water

indicators.note: in a down clue taking something up reads it upwards

explanation.surface: Someone sprayed by a jet of water, lifted up, narrowly got away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' reverses 'be', which goes 'in it', the jet word. The definition is literal: to emerge from a narrow place into open ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To debouch is to come out from a confined space such as a gorge into open country.

clue.text: One looks blank, being glued to a book

definitions.text: One looks blank, being glued to a book

parts.words: One looks blank, being glued to a book
parts.note: describes an empty page pasted at the front or back of a bound volume, though it suggests a bored reader

explanation.definitionFit: The blank page at the start or end of a book is partly pasted to its cover.

clue.text: Too fussy, following one year out of prison

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
nick is British slang for prison
Y is the abbreviation for year, here coming out of the prison and so after it

explanation.surface: Someone is overly fastidious after a year released from jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of prison' suggests release; it just puts the year after the jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overparticular about small details is the sense, synonym of fastidious.

clue.text: Pan-cooked food more healthy, doctor finally admitted

indicators.note: a piece admitted is let inside another

parts.note: fitter means in better health

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: The fried dish is healthier, the doctor at last conceded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' looks like conceded; it puts R inside FITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of batter-coated fruit or meat fried in a pan is a classic fried snack.

clue.text: Mess up climb, holding lead

indicators.note: to mess letters about is to jumble them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ruin a climb while taking the front position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess up' looks like one verb, but 'up' is fodder. 'lead' looks like being in front; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes compounds containing the metal, from Latin plumbum.

clue.text: Young animals fed with sweet are easily manipulated

definitions.note: an adjective phrase describing the answer, which is a plural noun: those who are easily manipulated

indicators.note: a piece fed with another has it put inside

parts.note: pups are young dogs or seals
pet, like sweet, is a term of endearment

explanation.surface: Baby animals given sweets are easy to control.
explanation.definitionFit: Marionettes on strings, and people controlled by others, are worked by someone else.

clue.text: Carlyle rewritten in easily understood style

indicators.note: the name is written out again with its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: The Victorian writer Carlyle revised for plain prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing plainly and lucidly means expressing something in a way that is simple to grasp.

clue.text: Star turn, say, included spicy concoction

indicators.note: the piece is included within another
a turned word is read backwards

parts.note: the sun is a star
e.g., for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: A headline variety act involves a spicy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star turn' looks like a headline act; 'turn' reverses SUN to NUS, which includes EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot drink of port or sherry with sugar and spice is named after Colonel Francis Negus.

clue.text: Composer's good fortune

parts.note: luck is fortune

explanation.surface: A musician's happy chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Christoph Willibald Gluck was an 18th-century German opera composer.

clue.text: Old saint is drawn into corrupt deception

indicators.note: the pieces are pulled inside the word that follows

parts.note: impure means corrupt or tainted

explanation.surface: An aged holy man is lured into a crooked fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretending to be someone else is a fraud or deceit.

clue.text: In yard, obtain English vegetable

indicators.note: the following piece is put in the yard

parts.note: a court is an enclosed yard
get means obtain

explanation.surface: Grow a home vegetable in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A zucchini, as Americans call it, is a small marrow.

clue.text: From which orifice does this vital fluid emerge?

indicators.note: the answer comes from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A question asking which opening a life fluid flows out of.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth, the fluid flowing in the veins of the gods is their blood.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth, the ethereal blood of the gods sustains their life.

clue.text: Servitude those defeated by Romans underwent

definitions.meaning: defeated Roman enemies were made to pass under an arch of spears

explanation.definitionFit: The frame on draught oxen stands for bondage; Rome humiliated beaten armies by marching them beneath one.

clue.text: Now for Christmas

definitions.meaning: December 25th, the day for giving gifts

explanation.definitionFit: The current era is the modern age; Christmas is the day for gifts.
